result.topic_en: Euler discusses which numbers occur among quadratic residues modulo primes, specifically showing that prime divisors of the forms $aa \pm nbb$ lie in certain linear forms $4nq \pm \alpha$, with arguments for the cases $\pm p$ modulo primes $4p+1$ and $4ffp+ii$, and a marginal note with numerical examples for $xx-2yy$.
result.transcription:
Tractatus de numerorum doctrina Cap. 10. 45
363. Ex § 346 sequitur, si $d$ et $e$ fuerint divisores cujuspiam numeri hujus formae $aa-nbb$, tum semper dari quadratum $xx$, ut $xx-ncc$ sit divisibile per numerum primum $4nq\pm deii$, quod quidem ex praecedente deduci posset, demonstrando si $aa-nbb$ habeat divisorem $d$, aliaque similis forma $ff-ngg$ divisorem $e$, dari etiam $hh-nkk$ divisibilem per productum $de$. Hoc patebit, si residua quadratorum, per numeros compositos divisorum, perpendemus.
364. Denique notatu dignum est, quod numerus $n$, ac propterea etiam $naa$ inter residua quadratorum occurrere nequeat, nisi divisor primus sit hujus formae $4nq+\alpha$, ubi $\alpha$ non omnes numeros ad $4n$ primos eoque minores significat, sed eorum tantum semissem, altera semisse penitus exclusa. Sicque omnes divisores primi formae $xx-naa$ talem habent formam $4nq+\alpha$, denotante $\alpha$ aliquot numeros, totidemque exclusis.
365. Similis est ratio numerorum formae $xx+naa$, cujus divisores primi adstringuntur ita ad formam $4nq+\alpha$, ut totidem numeri excludantur ab $\alpha$, quot admittuntur. Utroque autem casu omnia quadrata imparia $ii$ pro $\alpha$ valent, et si $\alpha$ valeat, etiam $\alpha ii$ valebit.
366. Ut demonstrationes has desideratas tentemus, consideremus divisorem primum $4p+1$, et cum duorum quadratorum summa $aa+bb$ exhiberi queat per eum divisibilis, ita ut alterum pro lubitu assumi possit, auferatur $(4p+1)bb$, eritque $aa-4pbb$ per $4p+1$ divisibile, seu dabitur quadratum $aa$, quod per $4p+1$ divisum relinquit $4pbb$, dabitur ergo quoque relinquens $p$, seu dabitur forma $aa-pbb$ per $4p+1$ divisibilis.
367. Cum etiam detur forma $aa-bb$ per $4p+1$ divisibilis, addendo $(4p+1)bb$, dabitur etiam talis forma $aa+pbb$ per $4p+1$ divisibilis, quae quidem jam inde patent, quod si quadrata per numerum primum $4p+1$ dividantur, in residuis tam $+p$ quam $-p$ reperiantur.
368. Sit autem divisor primus $4ffp+ii$, denotante $i$ numerum imparem, et quia tam forma $aa+bb$ quam $aa-bb$ per eum divisibilis exhiberi potest, hincque $iiaa+iibb$ et $iiaa-iibb$; inde auferendo, hinc vero addendo $(4ffp+ii)bb$, habebuntur formulae $iiaa-4ffpbb$ et $iiaa+4ffpbb$ per $4ffp+ii$ divisibiles, seu inter residua quadratorum erunt $\pm 4ffpbb$, ideoque etiam $\pm p$. Dabuntur ergo numeri tam hujus $xx+pyy$, quam hujus $xx-pyy$ formae per $4ffp+ii$ divisibiles. (*)
369. Si ergo concessis superioribus observationibus, divisor primus in quapiam harum formularum contineatur: $4rq+1$, $4rq+\alpha$, $4rq+\beta$, $4rq+\gamma$, $4rq+\delta$, etc., ubi numeri $1, \alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$, etc. sunt primi ad $4r$ eoque minores, quorum tamen tantum semissis hic occurrit, tum inter residua quadratorum certe occurrit numerus $r$; similique modo pro residuo $-r$ tales formulae divisorum habentur, quae cum illis conveniunt, si divisor sit formae $4p+1$, ab iis autem discrepant, si divisoris forma fuerit $4p-1$.
(*) Script. ad marg. Prius manifestum; nam $\frac{xx+pyy}{4ffp+ii}=$ int. si $x=i, y=2f$;
ut $xx-2yy$ divis. sit per 41, $x=7, 10, 13, 14, 17$
$y=2, 3, 8, 4, 1$
ut $xx-2yy$ divis. sit per 17,
$x=12, 5$ \quad $11, 6$ \quad $10, 7$ \quad $16, 1$ \quad $17, 4$
$y=2$ \quad $1$ \quad $4$ \quad $3$ \quad $5$.

methods.what: If $d$ and $e$ divide numbers of the form $aa-nbb$, some $xx-ncc$ is divisible by the prime $4nq\pm deii$, via multiplicativity of divisors of such forms
Prime divisors of $xx-naa$ (resp. $xx+naa$) lie in linear forms $4nq+\alpha$, with $\alpha$ ranging over exactly half of the residues coprime to $4n$
methods.quote: omnes divisores primi formae $xx-naa$ talem habent formam $4nq+\alpha$, denotante $\alpha$ aliquot numeros, totidemque exclusis

methods.what: Odd squares are admissible values of $\alpha$, and the admissible set is closed under multiplication by odd squares
methods.quote: omnia quadrata imparia $ii$ pro $\alpha$ valent, et si $\alpha$ valeat, etiam $\alpha ii$ valebit

methods.what: For a prime $4p+1$, $p$ is a quadratic residue (some $aa-pbb$ is divisible by it), derived from the divisibility of $aa+bb$
For a prime $4p+1$, both $+p$ and $-p$ are quadratic residues
For a prime $4ffp+ii$, $\pm p$ are quadratic residues, so it divides numbers of the forms $xx\pm pyy$
methods.quote: inter residua quadratorum erunt $\pm 4ffpbb$, ideoque etiam $\pm p$

methods.what: Explicit solution: $x=i, y=2f$ makes $xx+pyy$ divisible by $4ffp+ii$
Numerical solutions of $xx-2yy$ divisible by 41 and by 17
If a prime lies in the admissible forms $4rq+\alpha$, then $r$ is a quadratic residue; the forms for $-r$ agree for primes $4p+1$ and differ for primes $4p-1$
methods.quote: tum inter residua quadratorum certe occurrit numerus $r$

items.quote: quod quidem ex praecedente deduci posset, demonstrando si $aa-nbb$ habeat divisorem $d$, aliaque similis forma $ff-ngg$ divisorem $e$, dari etiam $hh-nkk$ divisibilem per productum $de$. Hoc patebit, si residua quadratorum, per numeros compositos divisorum, perpendemus.
items.english: which could indeed be deduced from the preceding, by showing that if $aa-nbb$ has divisor $d$ and another similar form $ff-ngg$ has divisor $e$, then there is also $hh-nkk$ divisible by the product $de$. This will become clear if we examine the residues of squares with respect to composite divisors.

items.quote: numerus $n$, ac propterea etiam $naa$ inter residua quadratorum occurrere nequeat, nisi divisor primus sit hujus formae $4nq+\alpha$, ubi $\alpha$ non omnes numeros ad $4n$ primos eoque minores significat, sed eorum tantum semissem
items.english: the number $n$, and hence also $naa$, cannot occur among the residues of squares unless the prime divisor is of the form $4nq+\alpha$, where $\alpha$ denotes not all numbers prime to and less than $4n$, but only half of them

items.quote: Similis est ratio numerorum formae $xx+naa$, cujus divisores primi adstringuntur ita ad formam $4nq+\alpha$, ut totidem numeri excludantur ab $\alpha$, quot admittuntur.
items.english: The case of numbers of the form $xx+naa$ is similar: their prime divisors are restricted to the form $4nq+\alpha$ in such a way that as many numbers are excluded from $\alpha$ as are admitted.
In order to attempt these desired demonstrations

items.quote: tum inter residua quadratorum certe occurrit numerus $r$; similique modo pro residuo $-r$ tales formulae divisorum habentur, quae cum illis conveniunt, si divisor sit formae $4p+1$, ab iis autem discrepant, si divisoris forma fuerit $4p-1$
items.english: then the number $r$ certainly occurs among the residues of squares; and similarly for the residue $-r$ there are such formulas for the divisors, which agree with those if the divisor is of the form $4p+1$, but differ from them if the divisor is of the form $4p-1$
